notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.
Train is a corridor level with a hostage standoff in the middle and a hard timer at the end. It is the level where positioning inside a single room decides whether an objective is possible at all.

nuance.claim: The level runs front to back through connected carriages with no branching, so there is no flanking and every fight is head-on down a narrow space.
The brake units are several separate targets, one per carriage, so the objective completes progressively as the train is worked through rather than at a single point.
nuance.because: Objective 0 names six separate destroy tags spread along the train.

nuance.claim: In the standoff room, moving to the far side before the dialogue starts opens a firing line on Ourumov that does not cross Natalya; from the doorway the shot is not available.
Ourumov holds Natalya and she dies to a stray shot, so the rescue is a single aimed shot rather than a firefight.
The standoff has a scripted opening and the shot has to be taken at the right moment in it, so the objective is a timing problem rather than an aiming one.
Cracking the password is required only on 00 Agent, so lower-difficulty routes skip the terminal entirely.
nuance.because: Objective 3's ObjectiveStart record carries the highest minimum difficulty in the level.

nuance.claim: Locating the secret base and cracking the password both happen in the rear compartment reached after the standoff, and both must be done before the escape begins.
nuance.because: Objective 4 is the level exit and objective 2 sits earlier in the difficulty chain.

nuance.claim: The escape runs on roughly a one minute countdown once it starts, which is not enough time to go back for anything missed.
During the escape guards fire from behind and stopping to return fire costs more than the damage taken; the run is made without engaging.
The exit from the rear compartment is cut through the floor rather than through a door, so a bot searching walls for an opening will not find one.
